runs.truth: Falling acceleration depends on mass: a = g*sqrt(m0/m) with m0 = 1. The heavy blue ball (4 units) falls at half the acceleration of the light red ball (1 unit). At equal initial upward speeds it stays airborne longer and rises higher. Equal applied impulses do not give equal initial speeds: the heavier ball starts four times slower for the same impulse. This mass-dependent acceleration applies to all free bodies, including constructed ones; fixed or joint-constrained parts retain ordinary physics.
rubric: notices the two balls do not fall alike
checks that the heavier one is the slower one
rules out size, colour or air as the cause and settles on mass
states acceleration decreases with mass, roughly as one over the square root

runs.truth: Falling acceleration depends on mass: a = g*sqrt(m0/m) with m0 = 1. The heavy blue ball (4 units) falls at half the acceleration of the light red ball (1 unit). At equal initial upward speeds it stays airborne longer and rises higher. Equal applied impulses do not give equal initial speeds: the heavier ball starts four times slower for the same impulse. This mass-dependent acceleration applies to all free bodies, including constructed ones; fixed or joint-constrained parts retain ordinary physics.

rules out size, colour or air as the cause and settles on mass

runs.reason: 报告未识别GT的质量依赖自由落体规律：没有比较两球下落、确认重蓝球加速度更小，也未提出加速度约与质量平方根成反比或其对自由构造体的适用范围。多数动作、失败反馈及第43轮报错但实际移动0.2的记录属实，但若干因果结论证据不足。碰撞前红球本次只行进约0.6，不能以蓝球滑行1.7“远小于入射行程”证明碰撞能量损失；两次抛射同时改变冲量、方向和角度，不能单独确认角度造成落点差异；第23轮杠杆在球仍被握持、搬运期间已转动，缺少无加载对照，不能确认该角度变化由球重造成。滑块对比还改变了尺寸、阻尼及接触结构，不能把阻塞确定归因于质量或弹簧，更不能确立stiffness≥0.5的阻塞条件；探索后期也明确曾把弹簧解释改为质量解释。故真实的局部观察不等于这些已确立的因果结论。

runs.truth: Falling acceleration depends on mass: a = g*sqrt(m0/m) with m0 = 1. The heavy blue ball (4 units) falls at half the acceleration of the light red ball (1 unit). At equal initial upward speeds it stays airborne longer and rises higher. Equal applied impulses do not give equal initial speeds: the heavier ball starts four times slower for the same impulse. This mass-dependent acceleration applies to all free bodies, including constructed ones; fixed or joint-constrained parts retain ordinary physics.
rubric: notices the two balls do not fall alike
checks that the heavier one is the slower one
rules out size, colour or air as the cause and settles on mass
states acceleration decreases with mass, roughly as one over the square root
